raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Description: Extend #6057’s separate grouped-expert FC1/FC2 prefetch chains to full-iteration and local CUDA graphs. Previously, captured expert weights shared the general graphed chain: current FC1 prefetched current FC2 instead of next-block FC1, reducing the available communication-overlap window. Additionally, recording gather completion when consumed could make current FC2 wait for unrelated later FC1 communication on the shared all-gather stream. ## This change: - Preserves independent captured FC1/FC2 chains and their buffer ownership. - Uses consistent captured-chain filtering for communication drains and stream joins. - Records grouped-gather completion immediately after issue, **after the underlying communication wait,** including synchronous fallbacks without a Work handle. - Replays gradient-ready hooks on each parameter’s actual reduce-scatter stream. ## Prefetch chains under full-iteration CUDA graphs BEFORE: one logical captured chain ``` [Dense] → [Grouped FC1] → [Grouped FC2] → [Dense] → ... all classified as GTP_graphed ``` AFTER: three logical captured chains ``` Dense: [Dense 0] → [Dense 1] → [Dense 2] → ... FC1: [FC1 L0] → [FC1 L1] → [FC1 L2] → ... FC2: [FC2 L0] → [FC2 L1] → [FC2 L2] → ... ``` The FC1/FC2 chains remain independent but share one AG stream. Each prefetch targets the same weight family in the next MoE block. ## Completion-event ordering and safety - **Steps 1–3:** the underlying `Work.wait()` establishes the NCCL → AG-stream dependency **before** recording the completion event. It does not insert a wait on the default stream. - **Steps 4–5:** the consumer still waits on that event before using the weights. - `completion_recorded=True` prevents re-recording the event at consumption, which would make it include unrelated later gathers. The later wrapper `wait()` only updates tracking state; its underlying Work handle has already been cleared. This preserves synchronization while allowing current FC2 computation to proceed without waiting for next-layer FC1 communication. ### Why this fix is critical for GTP+full-iter CG's performance - `Earlier prefetch`: The merged chain prefetches the next weight in execution order. Separate chains let FC1/FC2 prefetch their counterparts in the next MoE layer, giving communication more time to overlap computation. - `Fewer unnecessary waits`: The completion-event fix lets a GEMM start once its own weights arrive, without waiting for unrelated gathers queued afterward. - `CG makes this overlap more useful`: Full-iteration CG removes much of the CPU launch overhead. Better prefetching then helps keep the GPU compute stream busy instead of waiting for weights. ## Validation: - 89 targeted tests passed per rank on four GB300 GPUs: 80 basic GTP, 7 grouped-CG, and 2 partial-CG tests. - Covers BF16 full/local graph replay, eager/captured completion ordering, synchronous gather fallbacks, and native-MXFP8 SwiGLU replay across six Adam updates. - Fixed test isolation so captures do not join stale streams from earlier tests. ## Perf Results on DSV4-pro-half-proxy: 35% e2e perf gain Both runs use 256 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs, MXFP8, Adam, and the DSV4-Pro 30-layer proxy + MTP1, with TP1/PP1/CP1/EP64/**GTP64/EGTP4**, **full-iteration CUDA graphs**, and profiling enabled. | Run | GBS | MBS | Sequence length | Tokens/s/GPU | Model TFLOP/s/GPU | Step time (ms) | Peak allocated / sampled device memory (GiB) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Eager baseline | 512 | 2 | 4096 | 4,222.68 | 718.93 | 1,940.00 | 204.39 / 248.54 | | full-iter CG, w/o this MR | 512 | 2 | 4096 | 3,799.28 | 632.70 | 2,156.20 | 208.65 / 256.83 | | full-iter CG with this MR | 512 | 2 | 4096 | 5,146.16 | 857.00 | 1,591.87 | 210.30 / 257.81 | - Throughput improves by **35.45%** compared to CG case, , **19%** compared to eager mode. - Both runs use the same image, training arguments and profiling settings. The source difference consists of separate grouped-expert FC1/FC2 prefetch chains under CUDA graphs and recording gather completion before later prefetches. Related: #6057

The entire sync / buffer / chain architecture is shaped around making **captured fwd/bwd replays produce identical bit-for-bit behavior** — without the usual capture-vs-eager pitfalls that force other weight-sharding schemes to either disable CG or require special handling.
 
-- **Chains never cross-link across the capture axis** (`GTPChain.GRAPHED` / `GTPChain.UNGRAPHED`, plus the eager-only grouped-expert chains of §3.4). `prev_w` / `next_w` only connect same-chain params, so a captured traversal never reaches into eager Python and vice-versa.
+- **Chains never cross-link across the capture axis** (`GTPChain.GRAPHED` / `GTPChain.UNGRAPHED`, plus the separate grouped-expert FC1 and FC2 chains of §3.4). `prev_w` / `next_w` only connect same-chain params, so a captured traversal never reaches into eager Python and vice-versa.

 - **Idempotent ticket cache**: `GTPWeightCache.get(ticket)` keeps `slot.buf` set even after `release()`, so replays read the same buffer address as capture. `clear()` drops buffers while keeping tickets valid → supports CG re-capture with lazy re-allocation.

UNGRAPHED buffers stay in regular allocator memory.
